links.outcome: Readability (Flesch Reading Ease, Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level) of ChatGPT responses to urology patient questions
links.effect: Mean Flesch Reading Ease 35.5 (SD 10.2); mean Flesch-Kincaid Reading Grade Level 13.5 (1.74), i.e., college-level reading difficulty.
links.quote: The mean (SD) Flesch Reading Ease score was 35.5 (SD=10.2) and the mean Flesh-Kincaid Reading Grade Level score was 13.5 (1.74).

links.outcome: Whether ChatGPT outputs are comprehensible at patient-appropriate reading level
links.effect: Mean Flesch Reading Ease 35.5 and grade level 13.5, above typical patient literacy levels.
links.quote: The mean (SD) Flesch Reading Ease score was 35.5 (SD=10.2) and the mean Flesh-Kincaid Reading Grade Level score was 13.5 (1.74).

links.outcome: Appropriateness of ChatGPT responses including emergency-category urology questions, lacking vital information
links.effect: 14 of 18 (77.8%) responses appropriate; no significant difference across categories including emergency; low scores mostly due to missing, sometimes vital, information.
links.quote: The most common reason from urologists for low scores was responses lacking information-sometimes vital information.

screen.reason: Evaluates the accuracy, appropriateness, and readability of ChatGPT responses to urology patient questions without testing specific deployment practices or guardrails.
